questionText: Why has a statutory ban been imposed on amniocentesis in India?

options.text: To legally curb and prevent female foeticide resulting from prenatal sex determination
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: Because the amniotic fluid causes fatal allergic shock in mothers
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Because the amniotic fluid causes fatal allergic shock in mothers'.

options.text: Because it is completely incapable of detecting any chromosomal abnormalities
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Because it is completely incapable of detecting any chromosomal abnormalities'.

options.text: Because it triggers premature labour in 100% of pregnancies
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Because it triggers premature labour in 100% of pregnancies'.

detailedSolution:
1. A statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex-determination legally checks increasing menace of female foeticide.
2. Amniocentesis is a fetal sex determination and disorder test based on the chromosomal pattern in the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing embryo.
Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText: Which of the following statements correctly describes 'Saheli', the oral contraceptive pill developed in India?

options.text: It is a non-steroidal preparation taken once-a-week with high contraceptive value and very few side effects, developed by CDRI Lucknow
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: It is a high-dose daily progesterone-estrogen steroid pill
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'It is a high-dose daily progesterone-estrogen steroid pill'.

options.text: It is an injectable implant placed under the skin every 5 years
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'It is an injectable implant placed under the skin every 5 years'.

options.text: It is a spermicidal vaginal foam used immediately before coitus
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'It is a spermicidal vaginal foam used immediately before coitus'.

detailedSolution:
1. 'Saheli' – a new oral contraceptive for females – contains a non-steroidal preparation (centchroman).
2. It is a 'once a week' pill with very few side effects and high contraceptive value. It was developed by scientists at Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) in Lucknow.
Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText: Periodic abstinence is a natural contraceptive method wherein couples avoid or abstain from coitus from which days of the menstrual cycle when ovulation could be expected?

options.text: Day 10 to 17 of menstrual cycle
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: Day 1 to 5 of menstrual cycle
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Day 1 to 5 of menstrual cycle'.

options.text: Day 21 to 28 of menstrual cycle
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Day 21 to 28 of menstrual cycle'.

options.text: Day 24 to 28 of menstrual cycle
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Day 24 to 28 of menstrual cycle'.

detailedSolution:
1. Periodic abstinence is one such method in which the couples avoid or abstain from coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle when ovulation could be expected.
2. As chances of fertilization are very high during this period, it is called the fertile period.
Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText: Lactational amenorrhea (absence of menstruation during intense lactation) is effective as a natural contraceptive method up to a maximum period of:

options.text: Nearly 6 months following parturition
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: 24 months following parturition
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor '24 months following parturition'.

options.text: 1 month following parturition
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor '1 month following parturition'.

options.text: Indefinitely until weaning
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Indefinitely until weaning'.

detailedSolution:
1. This method is based on the fact that ovulation does not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition.
2. Therefore, as long as the mother breast-feeds the child fully, chances of conception are almost nil. However, this method has been reported to be effective only up to a maximum period of six months following parturition.
Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText: Condoms provide a dual advantage in reproductive health because:

options.text: They prevent pregnancy by blocking sperm deposition in the cervix and protect against sexually transmitted infections (STIs/AIDS)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: They inhibit ovulation permanently through hormone diffusion
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'They inhibit ovulation permanently through hormone diffusion'.

options.text: They induce permanent immunological sterility in the male
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'They induce permanent immunological sterility in the male'.

options.text: They cause lysis of the secondary oocyte upon contact
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'They cause lysis of the secondary oocyte upon contact'.

detailedSolution:
1. Condoms are barriers made of thin rubber/latex sheath used to cover the penis in the male or vagina and cervix in the female.
2. Its use has increased in recent years due to its additional benefit of protecting the user from contracting STIs and AIDS.
Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText:

List I                                | List II
--------------------------------------|--------------------------------------
(A)    Non-medicated IUD              | (I)    Progestasert and LNG-20

(C)    Hormone releasing IUD          | (III)  Diaphragm, cervical cap, and vaults

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly pairs each item in List I with its corresponding match in List II.

detailedSolution:

questionText: How do copper-releasing Intrauterine Devices (e.g., CuT, Multiload 375) primarily prevent conception?

options.text: Cu ions released suppress sperm motility and the fertilizing capacity of sperms
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: They block the fallopian tubes physically to prevent ovum release
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'They block the fallopian tubes physically to prevent ovum release'.

options.text: They destroy the corpus luteum within 24 hours of ovulation
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'They destroy the corpus luteum within 24 hours of ovulation'.

options.text: They prevent the surge of LH and FSH from anterior pituitary
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'They prevent the surge of LH and FSH from anterior pituitary'.

detailedSolution:
1. Cu ions released suppress sperm motility and the fertilizing capacity of sperms.
2. In addition, IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus.
Hence, Option A is correct.

1. The hormone releasing IUDs, in addition, make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to the sperms.
Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText: In molecular genetics analysis #151: During DNA replication, if RNA primers are synthesized by primase in the 5' -> 3' direction, why is an RNA primer mandatory for DNA polymerase to commence chain elongation?

options.text: DNA-dependent DNA polymerase cannot initiate DNA synthesis de novo and requires a free 3'-OH group to attach the incoming deoxynucleotide
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: RNA primer unwinds the double helix by breaking hydrogen bonds
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'RNA primer unwinds the double helix by breaking hydrogen bonds'.

options.text: RNA primer stabilizes the single-stranded DNA binding proteins
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'RNA primer stabilizes the single-stranded DNA binding proteins'.

options.text: DNA polymerase can only recognize ribose sugars at the active site
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'DNA polymerase can only recognize ribose sugars at the active site'.

detailedSolution:
1. DNA polymerases cannot initiate synthesis of a DNA strand de novo.
2. They require a pre-existing 3'-OH group (provided by the RNA primer synthesized by primase) to catalyze the formation of the phosphodiester bond.
Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText: In evolutionary biology study #61: Coelacanth (lobefin), caught in South Africa in 1938, was thought to be extinct. Why is the Coelacanth of immense evolutionary significance?

options.text: It represents the ancestor of modern amphibians that first crawled on land and evolved into terrestrial tetrapods
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: It is the direct ancestor of modern flying birds
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'It is the direct ancestor of modern flying birds'.

options.text: It is the oldest known mammal with placental nourishment
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'It is the oldest known mammal with placental nourishment'.

options.text: It provides fossil evidence of angiosperm pollination
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'It provides fossil evidence of angiosperm pollination'.

detailedSolution:
1. In 1938, a fish caught in South Africa happened to be a Coelacanth which was thought to be extinct.
2. These animals called lobefins evolved into the first amphibians that lived on both land and water.
Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText: In industrial biotechnology evaluation #91: Alcoholic beverages such as wine and beer are produced without distillation, whereas whisky, brandy, and rum are produced by distillation of the fermented broth. Why is distillation employed for the latter group?

options.text: Distillation increases the alcohol concentration because yeast cells are inhibited when alcohol content exceeds 13-14% during natural fermentation
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: Distillation eliminates toxic methanol completely
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Distillation eliminates toxic methanol completely'.

options.text: Distillation adds organic fruit flavours
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Distillation adds organic fruit flavours'.

options.text: Distillation introduces bacterial cultures for second fermentation
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Distillation introduces bacterial cultures for second fermentation'.

detailedSolution:
1. Wine and beer are produced without distillation whereas whisky, brandy and rum are produced by distillation of the fermented broth.
2. Natural fermentation ceases when yeast poisoning occurs at ~13% alcohol; distillation concentrates the ethanol to higher proof.
Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText: In molecular diagnostic testing #91: When using a radioactive single-stranded probe to detect a mutated gene in cloned host cells via autoradiography, why does the mutated gene NOT appear on the photographic film?

options.text: The radioactive probe cannot hybridize with the mutated gene because of lack of nucleotide sequence complementarity
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: The mutated gene emits gamma radiation that destroys the photographic emulsion
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'The mutated gene emits gamma radiation that destroys the photographic emulsion'.

options.text: The probe binds irreversibly to nitrocellulose membranes
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'The probe binds irreversibly to nitrocellulose membranes'.

options.text: The mutated gene is digested by host nucleases within the gel
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'The mutated gene is digested by host nucleases within the gel'.

detailedSolution:
1. A single stranded DNA or RNA, tagged with a radioactive molecule (probe) is allowed to hybridise to its complementary DNA in a clone of cells.
2. The clone having the mutated gene will hence not appear on the photographic film, because the probe will not have complementarity with the mutated gene.
Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText: Among the 'Evil Quartet' (the four major causes of biodiversity loss), which factor is recognized as the single most important cause driving animals and plants to extinction?

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Over-exploitation'.

options.text: Alien species invasions
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Alien species invasions'.

options.text: Co-extinctions
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Co-extinctions'.

questionText: Biodiversity hotspots are regions characterized by exceptionally high levels of species richness and high endemism. Which three hotspots cover India's high biodiversity regions?

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Aravalli Hills, Thar Desert, and Sunderbans'.

options.text: Eastern Ghats, Deccan Plateau, and Gangetic Plain
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Eastern Ghats, Deccan Plateau, and Gangetic Plain'.

options.text: Coromandel Coast, Malabar Coast, and Andaman Islands
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Coromandel Coast, Malabar Coast, and Andaman Islands'.

detailedSolution:

Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText: Which of the following is an ex-situ (off-site) biodiversity conservation method rather than in-situ?

options.text: Cryopreservation of gametes and Botanical gardens
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: National Parks
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'National Parks'.

options.text: Biosphere Reserves
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Biosphere Reserves'.

options.text: Wildlife Sanctuaries
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Wildlife Sanctuaries'.

detailedSolution:
1. In-situ (on site) conservation protects endangered species in their natural habitats (e.g. National Parks, Sanctuaries, Biosphere Reserves, Sacred Groves).
2. Ex-situ (off site) conservation takes threatened species out of their natural habitat into special care (Zoological parks, Botanical gardens, Wildlife safari parks, Cryopreservation, Seed banks).
Hence, Option A is correct.
